title: Probing the binding hypothesis of Smad3 modulators by molecular dynamic simulations for Atherosclerosis Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD).
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子动力学模拟和分子对接研究Smad3-FoxH1结合抑制剂的结合模式，属于蛋白质-DNA互作（转录因子Smad3与DNA结合辅因子FoxH1）体系，但聚焦小分子抑制剂而非TF-DNA直接结合建模，方法为物理模拟，可借鉴其MD流程于TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Transforming Growth Factor beta (TGFbeta) pathway has been recognized as one of the major processes involved in fibrotic diseases including the Atherosclerosis Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD). Many drugs have been proposed and are under clinical trials for modulation of the TGFbeta pathway by targeting TGFbeta receptor. Recently, various proof of the concept studies have advocated that the inhibition of TGFbeta-mediated Smad pathway could produce more focused effect with less off target toxicities in ASCVD. As these studies lack the mechanism and binding profile of Smad3 modulators, characterization of binding pattern for Smad3 inhibitors can provide a platform for the lead optimization against ASCVD. We utilized dimeric inhibitors from the PubChem dataset (PubChem ID: 630) of Smad3-FoxH1 binding inhibitors to generate binding hypothesis of Smad3 inhibitors. The selected compounds from the dataset were docked and ligand-protein complexes were simulated for 250 ns for further sampling of conformational space and to obtain stable binding hypothesis. Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD), Root Mean Square Fluctuation (RMSF) and hydrogen bond analysis of ligand-protein complexes after simulations revealed that Asn320 in Smad3 provides an efficient inhibition site for the two most potent small inhibitors (hereby named SM1 and SM2) of Smad3-FoxH1 binding. Although the diverse nature of compounds produce variable interaction patterns with FoxH1 binding site in Smad3, Gln315, Gln364 and Arg367 were observed to be the most common hydrogen bond interaction points in this binding site. Additionally, two compounds (hereby named SM8 and SM19) detached from the FoxH1 binding site and formed a highly stable complex around Tyr323 via hydrophobic complementarity, suggesting a new binding site for modulation of Smad3 activity.
abstract_zh: 转化生长因子β（TGFbeta）通路已被认为是涉及纤维化疾病（包括动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病（ASCVD））的主要过程之一。许多药物已被提出并正在进行临床试验，通过靶向TGFbeta受体来调节TGFbeta通路。近期，多项概念验证研究主张，抑制TGFbeta介导的Smad通路可能在ASCVD中产生更集中的效果，且脱靶毒性较低。由于这些研究缺乏Smad3调节剂的机制和结合谱，表征Smad3抑制剂的结合模式可为针对ASCVD的先导化合物优化提供平台。我们利用了PubChem数据集（PubChem ID: 630）中Smad3-FoxH1结合抑制剂的二聚体抑制剂，以生成Smad3抑制剂的结合假说。从数据集中选出的化合物进行了对接，并对配体-蛋白质复合物进行了250 ns的模拟，以进一步采样构象空间并获得稳定的结合假说。模拟后的配体-蛋白质复合物的均方根偏差（RMSD）、均方根波动（RMSF）和氢键分析显示，Smad3中的Asn320为两种最有效的小分子抑制剂（此处命名为SM1和SM2）对Smad3-FoxH1结合提供了有效的抑制位点。尽管化合物的多样性导致其与Smad3中FoxH1结合位点产生可变的相互作用模式，但观察到Gln315、Gln364和Arg367是该结合位点中最常见的氢键相互作用点。此外，两种化合物（此处命名为SM8和SM19）从FoxH1结合位点脱离，并通过疏水互补性在Tyr323周围形成高度稳定的复合物，提示存在一个调节Smad3活性的新结合位点。
